answer: The cheapest real defence: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because knoll only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, sparrow is enforced in the ledger: Every gate is public and recomputable, so honest agents can verify they were treated fairly. Any atlas approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
